Case_07004/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1. H and E stain of a bone marrow biopsy.

description.short_caption: H and E stain of a bone marrow biopsy showing cellular atypia and inclusions.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-power histopathology image of a bone marrow biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H and E). The field shows numerous cells with atypical morphology, including enlarged nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and cytoplasmic inclusions. There is a mix of cell types, with some appearing dysplastic. The background is cellular, consistent with bone marrow architecture.

Case_07004/figure2.jpg.source_caption: H and E stain of marrow, showing viral inclusion bodies (arrows).

description.short_caption: H&E stain of bone marrow showing viral inclusion bodies.
description.detailed_description: This is a high-magnification histopathology image of bone marrow stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The image shows numerous hematopoietic cells, with some cells containing prominent intranuclear viral inclusion bodies (indicated by arrows). These inclusions appear as dense, eosinophilic structures within the nuclei, consistent with a viral infection. The surrounding marrow architecture includes a mix of myeloid and erythroid precursors.
